newsitem.title: UK: BAe says can still make Eurofighter on time.
newsitem.headline: BAe says can still make Eurofighter on time.

text.p: British Aerospace Plc said on Thursday that there is still time to get the Eurofighter combat jet into production for first deliveries as planned in 2001, despite the further delays by Germany in approving the project.
Britain has already said it will buy 232 of the jets for the Royal Air Force (RAF) as its share of the launch order needed to get production programme underway.

"If production investment is available in the first quarter of next year then we can meet the deliveries due to the Royal Air Force (RAF) on time in 2001, for squadron service in 2002," said a spokesman for BAe.

The German goverment has been holding up the go-ahead for the project because of cuts in its defence budget and is not now expected to make a decision on funding its share of the production investment programme for Eurofighter until next year.

The Eurofighter consortium of British Aerospace, Daimler Benz Aerospace, Italy's Alenia and Spain's Casa had hoped their governments would have a memorandum of understanding for production investment by the end of 1997.
Although BAe says Eurofighter can still be produced on time industry sources said it is getting concerned that further delays will mean Eurofighter misses out on export sales.
The four member governments are expected to give a launch order for around 620 aircraft but senior BAe executives have said they see opportunities to sell 300 to 400 more aircraft overseas.

"Of course we are particularly keen to establish the aircraft in the export market," a company official said on Thursday. "We believe there is a potential for exports not only in Europe but in the Middle East and the Asia Pacific region."
